name: Speak
description: Read text aloud to the user through a swappable speech backend. Tools: Speak, SpeakStatus, SpeakStop.

tool.name: Speak
tool.description: Speak text aloud to the user through the computer's speakers, in a clear professional voice. Use it to read out an answer, announce that a long task finished, deliver a short alert, or narrate anything the user asked to hear instead of read. Speech plays in the background and the tool returns immediately with a short job handle (e.g. `s1`); the user hears it while you keep working. Poll `SpeakStatus` to see whether a job is still talking, and `SpeakStop` to cut it off (for example if the user says "stop" or you spoke the wrong thing). Speaking does not interrupt the conversation. Keep spoken text natural: prefer plain sentences over markdown, code blocks, or long URLs, which sound bad read aloud.

text.description: The text to read aloud. Plain prose works best. Markdown syntax, code, and raw URLs are read literally and sound bad, so paraphrase them into speech-friendly wording first. Max 8000 characters.

wait.description: When false (default), return immediately with a job handle and let the speech play in the background while you continue. When true, block until the speech finishes (or the per-call time budget is hit) before returning. Use `true` only for a short line you want confirmed as fully spoken before you move on; never for long passages, which would stall the turn.

tool.name: SpeakStatus
tool.description: Report whether speech is currently playing. Pass a job handle (e.g. `s1`) from a prior Speak call to check that one job, or omit `id` to list every speech job this session and its state (speaking, done, failed, or stopped). Cheap and read-only. Use it before deciding whether to wait, speak again, or stop an in-flight job.

id.description: A speech job handle returned by Speak (e.g. `s1`). Omit to get the state of all jobs in this session.

tool.name: SpeakStop
tool.description: Stop speech that is currently playing. Pass a job handle (e.g. `s1`) from a prior Speak call to silence just that job, or omit `id` to stop every active speech job at once (the "be quiet now" button). Stopping a job that already finished is a no-op and is reported as such. Use this the moment the user says to stop, or when you realize you spoke the wrong thing.

id.description: A speech job handle returned by Speak (e.g. `s1`). Omit to stop every active speech job in this session.
